edits.html:
Missed DDH DDH (developmental dysplasia of the hip) is a poorly developed acetabulum that leaves the femoral head unstable. Untreated, it leads to disability, pain and early osteoarthritis. How NBME framed it: every option was a disease written as its mechanism, and the stem gave a walker's signs instead of Barlow or Ortolani.
True-fact-wrong-slotDisplacement of the capital femoral epiphysis — this is slipped capital femoral epiphysis stated as a mechanism. It affects adolescents and limits hip internal rotation.
True-fact-wrong-slotFailure of osteoid to mineralize — this is rickets stated as a mechanism. Vitamin D deficiency bows both legs; it does not shorten one leg or limit one hip.
Unchecked attributeAcute epiphyseal fracture — a growth plate fracture follows trauma and causes pain, bruising and guarding. This limp is painless and has lasted 4 months.
Unchecked attributeAcute suppurative arthritis — septic arthritis brings fever, joint pain and lost motion. This child is healthy with a painless limp for 4 months.
Unchecked attributeAvulsion of muscle origin — an avulsion follows an injury and is painful, often with a palpable defect or mass. This history has no injury and no pain.
